channel.title: Lecture Videos on MIT OpenCourseWare
channel.description: Recent content in Lecture Videos on MIT OpenCourseWare

item.title: Lecture 1: Interactive Proofs and the Sum-Check Protocol, Part 1
item.description: This lecture covers topics including definition of interactive proofs (IP), the sum-check protocol, and the application of interactive proof for #SAT.

item.title: Lecture 1: Interactive Proofs and the Sum-Check Protocol, Part 2
item.description: This lecture continues the topics including definition of interactive proofs (IP), the sum-check protocol, and the application of interactive proof for #SAT.

item.title: Lecture 2: Doubly Efficient Interactive Proofs, Part 1
item.description: This lecture covers topics including definition and examples of doubly efficient IP for counting triangles in a graph, low-degree extension, and doubly efficient IP for all bounded depth computations (the GKR protocol).

item.title: Lecture 2: Doubly Efficient Interactive Proofs, Part 2
item.description: This lecture continues the topics including definition and examples of doubly efficient IP for counting triangles in a graph, low-degree extension, and doubly efficient IP for all bounded depth computations (the GKR protocol).

item.title: Lecture 3: Continuation of the GKR Protocol and Corollaries
item.description: This lecture covers the topic of IP = PSPACE and its application.

item.title: Lecture 4: PCP via GKR and Interactive Arguments, Part 1
item.description: This lecture covers topics including  the probabilistically checkable proofs (PCP), definition and construction from GKR and the interactive succinct argument for NP.

item.title: Lecture 4: PCP via GKR and Interactive Arguments, Part 2
item.description: This lecture continues the topics including the probabilistically checkable proofs (PCP), definition and construction from GKR and the interactive succinct argument for NP.

item.title: Lecture 5: The Kilian-Micali Protocol, Part 1
item.description: This lecture discusses how to use collision-resistant hash (CRH) functions with local openings and PCP to construct interactive arguments.

item.title: Lecture 5: The Kilian-Micali Protocol, Part 2
item.description: This lecture continues the discussion on how to use collision-resistant hash (CRH) functions with local openings and PCP to construct interactive arguments.

item.title: Lecture 6: Fiat-Shamir Paradigm and Zero-Knowledge Proofs, Part 1
item.description: This lecture covers the topics of proving the Merkel hash is collision resistant, eliminating interaction via the Fiat-Shamir paradigm, and proving the soundness of the Kilian-Micali protocol in ROM.

item.title: Lecture 6: Fiat-Shamir Paradigm and Zero-Knowledge Proofs, Part 2
item.description: This lecture continues the topics of proving the Merkel hash is collision resistant, eliminating interaction via the Fiat-Shamir paradigm, and proving the soundness of the Kilian-Micali protocol in ROM.

item.title: Lecture 7: Soundness of the Fiat-Shamir Paradigm in the Standard Model, Part 1
item.description: This lecture covers topics including the definition of CI hash functions, existence in the ROM and simple counter example in the plain model.

item.title: Lecture 7: Soundness of the Fiat-Shamir Paradigm in the Standard Model, Part 2
item.description: This lecture continues the topics including the definition of CI hash functions, existence in the ROM and simple counter example in the plain model.

item.title: Lecture 8: Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments for Batch NP (BARGs) from LWE, Part 1
item.description: This lecture covers batch NP (BARGs) from learning with errors (LWE), including the local somewhere statistically binding (SSB) with local opening and probabilistically checkable proof (PCP) with fast online verification.

item.title: Lecture 8: Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments for Batch NP (BARGs) from LWE, Part 2
item.description: This lecture continues batch NP (BARGs) from learning with errors (LWE), including the local somewhere statistically binding (SSB) with local opening and probabilistically checkable proof (PCP) with fast online verification.

item.title: Lecture 9: BARGs Implies SNARGs and Connection to Non-Signaling PCPs, Part 1
item.description: This lecture covers topics including BARGs implies SNARGs and connection to non-signaling PCPs.

item.title: Lecture 9: BARGs Implies SNARGs and Connection to Non-Signaling PCPs, Part 2
item.description: This lecture continues the topics including BARGs implies SNARGs and connection to non-signaling PCPs.
